land.text: the Greek states of the league, now held by Antipater's Macedon after the Lamian War

successors.note: The infobox names the Macedonian Empire as successor. macedonian-empire's dossier takes the Greeks back as vassals in 322.

capitals.name: Pella
capitals.note: The infobox gives Pella as capital; the page puts the organizing of the league near Corinth ('In mid 337 BC, he seems to have camped near Corinth'). Pella's coordinates.

rulers.name: Philip II (hegemon)
rulers.title: hegemon and strategos autokrator
rulers.note: The infobox lists the hegemons as Philip II (338/337 BC), Alexander III the Great (336 BC), Demetrius I Poliorcetes (304 BC) and Antigonus III Doson (224 BC).

rulers.name: Alexander the Great (hegemon)
rulers.title: hegemon
rulers.note: He 'revived his father's League of Corinth' in 336 (the infobox gives him as hegemon from 336 BC); the page gives no end for his hegemony, so the strip runs to the dissolution of the League in 322. Antipater was deputy hegemon during the Asian campaign (undated on the page).

region.text: the Greek states that accepted the settlement 'with the exception of Sparta': Thessalians, Phocians, Locrians, Malians, Thasians, Samothracians, Ambraciots, Perrhaebi, Zacynthus, Cephalenia and others

ledger.note: 337: Philip II founds the League of Corinth. Philip II created the federation in 338-337 BC (the page: 'created by Philip II of Macedon') after Chaeronea; 'In mid 337 BC, he seems to have camped near Corinth', where he began organizing the league; the infobox gives it as established 338/337 BC. An association (rule 4), never territory.
336: Alexander takes the hegemony. Alexander III took the throne in 336 BC and 'revived his father's League of Corinth', using it to plan the invasion of Asia.

region.text: the Greek states of the league

ledger.note: 322: the League ends. 'The League was dissolved after the Lamian War in 322 BC' (the infobox gives it as disestablished 322 BC). Its Greek members pass to Macedonian control (macedonian-empire's 322 vassalage).

wars.name: Lamian War
wars.outcome: 'The League was dissolved after the Lamian War in 322 BC'. The Hellenic League of the war is athenian-coalition's dossier.
wars.note: The page gives only the end date 322 and names no belligerents; the span 322 is the page's date and the belligerents are those of the macedonian-empire and athenian-coalition dossiers.

certainty.note: An association with no territory of its own; the page gives no territorial extent.

sources.title: League of Corinth
sources.note: Founding 338/337, members and Sparta's refusal, Alexander's renewal 336, Megalopolis 331, dissolution 322, the revivals of 306-301 and 224.

sources.title: Demetrius I of Macedon
sources.note: Cited in the notes only: 'In 304 BC, he returned a second time to Greece as liberator, and reinstated the Corinthian League'.

notes: One page, which dates the whole life. Type umbrella: a federation of Greek states under a Macedonian hegemon, never territory (rule 4), so there are no keyframes (as in latin-league). The infobox gives established 338/337 and disestablished 322; the start here is mid-337, when the league was organised at Corinth. Revivals the page names but this dossier does not give a second life: Antigonus I and Demetrius 'attempted to recreate Philip II's Hellenic league' after Salamis (306), Demetrius 'reinstated' it in 304 (the Demetrius I of Macedon page, already cited by antigonid-dynasty; the League page gives no 302 date) and it ended with Ipsus (301); Antigonus III Doson 'revived the Hellenic League' in 224, now called the Hellenic Alliance, including the Achaeans, Thessalians, Boeotians and others (page, paraphrased) and lasting at least to Sellasia (222), with no end date on the page. A reviewer who wants the three lives should split them into dossiers. Not on the page: the date and fact of Thebes's destruction by the council (335), the membership list's date, Sparta's actual entry. The 331 gain is an event of the page's wording (Sparta's request on the condition that it join), at confidence 2. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: the 331 'gain' of Sparta from peloponnesian-league was removed: the page says only that Sparta's appeal was 'agreed on condition that the Lacedaemonians now joined the League of Corinth' and does not say Sparta joined; an umbrella holds no territory, and peloponnesian-league keeps Sparta to 192]
